findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)', not a Cisco ACI add-on. The Cisco ACI add-on is TA_cisco-ACI (Splunkbase 1897, deprecated), and Cisco now points users to Cisco DC Networking (Splunkbase 7777). The same wrong ID appears in dataSources and in the references list.
findings.suggested_fix: Name Cisco DC Networking (cisco_dc_networking_app_for_splunk, Splunkbase 7777) as the supported collector, with TA_cisco-ACI (Splunkbase 1897, deprecated) as the legacy option. Remove every '4022' reference from app, dataSources and references.

findings.explanation: This reference URL points to the Cisco homepage, not a document. Separately, the 'Splunk Add-on for Cisco ACI (Splunkbase 4022)' entry links to an Nmon add-on.
findings.quote: {"title": "Cisco APIC Operations Guide — Monitoring Tenants and fabric (Release 6.0(x))", "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"}
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the placeholder with the specific APIC guide URL, or drop it. Point the add-on reference at https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7777 (or 1897 for the legacy TA).

findings.explanation: APIC has no fvFaultInst class. Active faults are faultInst objects, and they come back as EPG children via rsp-subtree-include=faults. The same invented class is used in the REST query in detailedImplementation Step 1 (target-subtree-class=fvCEp,fvFaultInst,healthInst) and in later paragraphs.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace fvFaultInst with faultInst everywhere. Build the query as GET /api/class/fvAEPg.json?rsp-subtree-include=health,faults (or target-subtree-class=fvCEp,faultInst,healthInst with query-target=subtree).

findings.explanation: rsp-prop-include accepts only all, naming-only or config-only. To get health with an object, use rsp-subtree-include=health.
findings.suggested_fix: Use ?rsp-subtree-include=health (optionally ,no-scoped) on the EPG MO query.

findings.explanation: Only F0467 (invalid-vlan / invalid-path / encap-already-in-use against an EPG) is an EPG deployment fault. F1394 is a leaf-to-spine fabric port going down, and Cisco describes F1545 as a cosmetic atomic-counter packet-drop fault, so neither indicates EPG health.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep F0467 and replace F1394/F1545 with EPG-scoped fault codes looked up in the APIC fault catalogue, or explain that F1394 is a fabric-level corroboration signal.

findings.explanation: The NDI endpoint path and an APIC gRPC 'epg-health' sensor look invented. I could not find either in Cisco documentation.
findings.quote: Nexus Dashboard Insights **`GET https://<nd-insights>/sedgeapi/v1/site_health`** per-site widgets; optional **gRPC** **epg-health** streaming telemetry from APIC
findings.suggested_fix: Check the Nexus Dashboard Insights API reference for the actual site/EPG health endpoint, and confirm whether APIC supports gRPC telemetry export. Remove both if they cannot be confirmed.

findings.explanation: The shipping Cisco add-ons emit cisco:dc:aci:health / cisco:dc:aci:class / cisco:dc:aci:stats (Cisco DC Networking) or cisco:apic:* (legacy TA), not cisco:aci:*. actrlPermitStats/actrlDropStats are not documented APIC class names; per-rule hit counters are actrlRuleHit5min and similar.
findings.suggested_fix: Either state clearly that cisco:aci:* sourcetypes come from a custom collector, or switch to the sourcetypes the Splunkbase 7777 app actually produces. Confirm the actrl stats class names in the APIC MIM reference.

findings.explanation: The CIM Performance datamodel covers host CPU, memory, storage, network interface, OS and uptime metrics, not ACI EPG health scores or contract counters. The SPL does not use any datamodel.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop Performance (and keep Inventory only if the EPG inventory is actually mapped), or set cimModels to empty and say the UC runs on raw sourcetypes.

findings.explanation: implementation, detailedImplementation and the SPL each give different paging thresholds. The SPL uses fds_latest>=9 OR (fds_latest>=6 AND slo_pct<99.9) OR slo_pct<99 OR ep_anomaly, and nothing in it checks health_score<85.
findings.quote: implementation: "fault_density_score≥9 or slo_pct<99"; detailedImplementation quick win: "fds_latest≥6 OR slo_pct<99"; runbook: "fault_density_score crosses weighted thresholds while health_score<85"
findings.suggested_fix: State one threshold set that matches the SPL in implementation, in the detailedImplementation quick win, and in the runbook.

findings.explanation: These are divide-by-zero guards and the healthy-slice test, not alert conditions. hs >= 90 is the healthy state, so this reads as the opposite of the detection.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the real alert conditions: slo_pct below 99, an endpoint-count swing beyond +40%/-35%, or a weighted fault density of at least 9 (or at least 6 with SLO below 99.9).

findings.explanation: No crash_band field exists in the SPL or the data sources, and ACI health scores have no 'crash bands' (detailedImplementation also mentions 'Cisco crash bands').
findings.suggested_fix: Use the health score with a stated colour threshold (for example under 90 amber, under 70 red) instead of crash_band.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified by an automated agent, with no SME sign-off, and its SPL does not run as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/unverified until a human SME has run the search against APIC data.

findings.explanation: The trailing paragraphs (stretched-fabric hygiene, capacity planners, documentation packs, RBA adapters) are filler built from undefined terms. They do not help anyone implement this detection, and they repeat the Step 4/6 content.
findings.quote: plus CMDB-backed owner attestations referencing DaC label completeness whenever Endpoint-as-Data-Class audits accompany microSeg onboarding waves.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the free-floating paragraphs after Step 5 and keep the numbered steps tied to the actual SPL.

findings.explanation: The SPL does not check bridge-domain subnets. It uses health score, endpoint count, fault counts and contract drop ratio.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the subnet clause with 'and how many problems the controller has raised against it'.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `eval slo_degraded=isnull(slo_pct) OR slo_pct<99 OR ...` assigns a boolean expression to a field. Splunk rejects this ('The result of an eval expression cannot be a Boolean'), so the search errors out before `where slo_degraded=1`. Wrap it in if(..., 1, 0).

`slo_pct=round(100*hs_good/days_seen,3)` divides a count of healthy 5-minute slices (up to 288 per day) by the number of days, so values reach about 28,800 instead of a percentage, and slo_pct<99 fires only when almost no slices are healthy. The denominator should be the total interval count (sum of `intervals`).

`rex field=fv_dn "/uni/tn-(?<tenant_name>...)"` requires a leading slash, but ACI dn attributes start with 'uni/tn-...' (see the guide's cisco:aci:health sample `"dn": "uni/tn-tenant-retail/health"`), so tenant/app/EPG names are never extracted. Health dn values also end in '/health' and contract-stat dn values are not EPG paths, so the three sourcetypes never merge on fv_dn.

endpoint_count and the fault counts coalesce to "0" on events that lack them (every health and contract event), so min(ep_cnt) is usually 0, ep_chg_pct is null, and the endpoint-anomaly branch never fires.
T1078 (Valid Accounts) has no relationship to an EPG availability/health score detection.

summary: The EPG-health idea is sound, but the UC names the wrong Splunkbase add-on, invents APIC classes and query options, and ships SPL that cannot run (it assigns a boolean in eval) and computes a meaningless SLO percentage. Thresholds disagree across the implementation fields, and the CIM mapping does not fit the signal.
